references.text: Describes how the Danites took the cultic objects that Micah had made, along with his priest, whom they now bring with them to Laish.
The scouts described Laish as a people who lived securely and carelessly, which now makes them vulnerable to the Danites' attack.
God's command to strike the inhabitants of a city with the sword and burn the city with fire, the same fate that befalls Laish.
Jericho was burned with fire after its conquest, a similar pattern of destruction that the Danites used against Laish.
Joshua struck the inhabitants of Hazor with the sword, a similar expression of total military victory.
Judah conquered Jerusalem and struck the city with the sword and set it on fire, the same type of warfare as against Laish.
The Israelites set fire to the cities in Benjamin, destruction similar to what the Danites carried out against Laish.
